failure_patterns.pattern: rule_missing: Returned a named example instead of the role it exemplified.

rejected_edits.content: - Use the context-supported conventional form of a name or answer, and include additional name parts or modifiers only when the clue requires them or they distinguish otherwise-confusable entities. As a final exact-match check, remove any unnecessary given name, organization suffix, subtitle, or descriptive qualifier; if the shorter canonical form still uniquely fills the requested slot, return that form. Do not expand a conventional short name or title into a longer official form solely because the context displays it.
rejected_edits.target: - Use the context-supported conventional form of a name or answer, and include additional name parts only when needed to distinguish otherwise-confusable entities.

rejected_edits.content: - In trivia or wordplay clues, treat a parenthetical number as a hard answer-length constraint. For a double-definition clue (for example, “X, or what Y is put to”), seek the exact word that fits both senses rather than a synonym that fits only one. Use a proper-name cue to identify a name only when the requested slot is a name or name part. If a name is introduced as an example (“like X”) to signal a shared role or category, return that role or category, not the example’s name.
rejected_edits.target: - In trivia or wordplay clues, treat a parenthetical number as a hard answer-length constraint. For a double-definition clue (for example, “X, or what Y is put to”), seek the exact word that fits both senses rather than a synonym that fits only one. Use any proper-name cue to identify the requested name or name part.
